# Platform and Organism Assignment of GEO Series GSE309890

## Abstract

This report resolves two metadata attributes of a single Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series record, GSE309890: the sequencing platform on which it was run, and the organism profiled. The GEO record was fetched by accession through the NCBI E-utilities `esummary` endpoint against the `gds` database (UID 200309890), and the platform identifier returned by that record was then resolved as a second GEO record (GPL24659, UID 100024659). GSE309890 is a Series of experiment type "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" comprising 6 samples (3 control replicates, 3 adaptive-evolution 40-day replicates), registered under BioProject PRJNA1363958, with a public date of 2026/02/01. The taxon field of the Series is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, and the single platform field value is GPL24659. The GPL24659 record titles that platform "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)", public since 2018/02/26 and used by 460 samples in total across GEO. The two records agree on the organism. No PubMed record is linked to either the Series or the Platform, so no publication could be cited. The result matters because platform and taxon determine whether the Series can be pooled with other datasets for reanalysis.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is a bacterial transcriptomic Series whose stated subject is the effect of the SSRI sertraline on antibiotic resistance emergence in *Escherichia coli*, with a focus on rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway and the role of transketolase A (tktA). Platform identity fixes the read technology and read characteristics; organism identity fixes the reference genome and annotation needed to interpret the supplied FPKM matrix. Both are prerequisites for reuse.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The GEO tool reported for both GSE309890 and GPL24659: "No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record," with `pubmed_ids` empty in each case.

**Knowledge Gap.** The accession alone carries no platform or taxon information; GEO Series records store the platform as a GPL identifier that is itself opaque until resolved to a second record.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: report the `platform` and `taxon` fields of GSE309890, and resolve the platform identifier to an instrument name. Expectation: the taxon recorded on the Series and on its Platform record agree.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The question is a direct metadata lookup on a known accession, so no search step was used. Accession-based retrieval was routed to the GEO tool, which validates the returned record against the accession requested. The Platform value returned by the first call determined the second call, so the calls were run in sequence, not in parallel.

**Materials.** NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, reached via the `geo_series` tool, which queries E-utilities `esummary.fcgi` against the `gds` database.

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)` — resolved to `db=gds, id=200309890, version=2.0`; returned Series metadata plus the FTP supplementary listing.
2. `geo_series(accession="GPL24659", list_files=false)` — resolved to `db=gds, id=100024659, version=2.0`; the GPL value was taken verbatim from the `platform` field of call 1. File listing was disabled because only the platform title was needed.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. Each reported value is a single field copied from one record: `platform`, `taxon`, `sample_count`, `experiment_type`, `date_public`, `bioproject` from the GSE record, and `title`, `taxon`, `sample_count`, `date_public` from the GPL record. The sample count of 6 is the `sample_count` field and is matched by 6 entries in the `samples` array; no deduplication was required. No percentages are reported, so no denominator applies.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Fields returned for GSE309890 (Series, UID 200309890).**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Accession | GSE309890 |
| Entry type | GSE (Series) |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Taxon | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Sample count | 6 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | none registered |
| Supplementary file types | CSV |

**Table 2. Fields returned for GPL24659 (Platform, UID 100024659).**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Accession | GPL24659 |
| Entry type | GPL (Platform) |
| Title | Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655) |
| Taxon | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Public date | 2018/02/26 |
| Samples using this platform | 460 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | none registered |

**Table 3. Samples listed in GSE309890.**

| Sample accession | Title |
|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control, rep1 |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control, rep2 |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control, rep3 |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |

**Findings.** GSE309890 lists one platform, GPL24659, whose record title is "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)". The organism recorded on the Series is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The Platform record carries the same taxon string. The Series contains 6 samples in two groups of 3. The Series is registered under BioProject PRJNA1363958. GPL24659 has been public since 2018/02/26 and is associated with 460 samples across GEO; GSE309890 has a public date of 2026/02/01. Neither record has a linked PubMed ID. The Series has one supplementary file, GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz, 510K, last modified 2025-11-14.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Both objectives are met by direct field retrieval: the platform is Illumina HiSeq 4000 (GPL24659) and the organism is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The hypothesis that the Series taxon and Platform taxon agree is supported — both records carry the identical taxon string, which is expected because GEO Platform records are organism-specific instances of an instrument.

**Context.** The platform and experiment type are mutually consistent: "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" on a HiSeq 4000 is RNA-seq, and the supplementary file is an FPKM matrix, an RNA-seq quantification. The six-sample, two-group design (control versus 40-day adaptive evolution) matches the Series summary's account of a sertraline-driven adaptive evolution experiment in *E. coli*.

**Limitations.** The GEO tool states that E-utilities returns metadata only: processed expression values exist solely in the FTP supplementary file and were not retrieved or inspected here, so nothing in this report speaks to the expression data itself. The tool further notes that an absent PubMed link means no link is registered in GEO — typically an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study — and never that the study has no data; the sertraline and tktA claims quoted from the Series summary are the submitter's own text and were not independently verified. The Platform title names the instrument model as the submitter registered it; read length, chemistry, and library protocol are not in the `esummary` record. The 460-sample figure for GPL24659 counts all GEO samples on that platform, not samples in this Series. The public date of 2026/02/01 indicates the record is under a submitter hold and its metadata may still change.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 was run on Illumina HiSeq 4000 (GPL24659) and profiles *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The next query worth running is a retrieval of the raw runs behind BioProject PRJNA1363958 to confirm the instrument at the run level and obtain read counts and FASTQ links, since the GEO Platform title reports the model as declared rather than as recorded per run.

## References

[1] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, Series GSE309890 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, Platform GPL24659 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659
[3] NCBI E-utilities esummary endpoint (db=gds), used for both records — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[4] GEO FTP directory for GSE309890 — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[5] GEO FTP supplementary file, GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[6] GEO FTP directory for GPL24659 — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/platforms/GPL24nnn/GPL24659/

## Acknowledgments

Records were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and retrieved through NCBI E-utilities, National Center for Biotechnology Information, U.S. National Library of Medicine. The underlying Series and sample metadata were deposited by the submitters of GSE309890 and BioProject PRJNA1363958.
